title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Geneva Grid for the expert question page. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Geneva Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style, Geneva and Zurich, 1950s-60s
options.thesis: Each question set like a Swiss information poster: objective grotesk on one strict grid, so the same unit transposes cleanly into WhatsApp, email and embed.
options.viewport: Yellow shell band with wordmark and anonymity status; the question in large grotesk owns the screen; full-width Yes / No / Don't know; R1043 risk strip folded below.
options.risk: Swiss restraint tips into cold bureaucracy if the yellow band and type scale are set timidly.

raised.raise: Proof beside every rating: ACAPS probability and impact always carry their rationale line, source and date, never a bare chip.
Three type sizes only; rank carried by weight, case and reversal. The chosen answer is the screen's single reversed black plate.
One cell grid drives the page, the share card and the embed, so transposition between media is exact, cell for cell.
One element dominates each screen: the question owns the first viewport and everything else sits visibly below it.
Full state vocabulary, each its own mark: selected, sent, pending ACAPS review (hollow), queued offline, failed.
No grey words: all reading text holds near-black on paper for sunlight legibility; grey is for rules only.

options.label: Secret Ballot
options.lineage: Secret ballot paper with numbered counterfoil
options.thesis: Answering is casting a secret ballot: the counterfoil with your identity stays with ACAPS, the ballot travels anonymous.
options.viewport: Ballot-tinted question card with a numbered stub split off by a perforation; three boxed answer marks; risk context below.
options.risk: Electoral connotation suggests majority vote rather than expert judgement; security texture can slide into costume.

options.label: Monochrome Product Canon
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white, one accent, every claim paired with proof.
options.viewport: Grey question card, hairline ghost buttons, one accent submit.
options.case: Fuses as the grey-plus-one-accent default; experts recognise nothing of their world in it.
options.kept: Claim paired with proof: every rating shown with its rationale.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case, reversal and rule.
options.viewport: Raked slides of question and context along a lateral rack.
options.case: Raked containers fight a one-tap answer; airline nostalgia has no tie to field experts.
options.kept: Rank by weight and reversal; one reversed plate per screen.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Question number built from grid cells over faint blue gridlines.
options.case: Visible construction reads as a type exercise, not a trusted question; close kin to the assigned world but less clear.
options.kept: One cell grid governs every rendering of the unit.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Swelling lobes of flat colour, capsule controls, overshoot motion.
options.viewport: A green lobe carrying the question with coral and yellow capsules.
options.case: Playful leisure register is wrong for crisis risk; loses on both axes.

options.label: Manual Acetate Tab Board
options.thesis: Acetate leaves over a full-hue divider board, stepped tab rail.
options.viewport: Question on an acetate leaf over a chrome-yellow board with a tab rail.
options.case: Ply metaphor adds a layer experts must decode; no tie to their world.
options.kept: Every state its own physical mark, pending included.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.viewport: Question over a strobing bar field with packed numerals.
options.case: Strobing data-art is hostile to field use and trust; loses on both axes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The humanitarian survey form: white cards, UN-style blue, one question per screen, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Logo header, question card, three pill buttons, sticky submit bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every survey tool experts already ignore.
